# unifi_console_certificate (Resource)

A TLS certificate installed on the **UniFi OS console itself** (the unifi-core management UI, e.g. `https://192.0.2.1`) — replacing the self-signed default with a Let's Encrypt certificate (native ACME, automated DNS-01) or an uploaded BYO certificate.

For `letsEncrypt`, the **console owns renewal**: Terraform performs the initial issuance and hands the credentials to the device, which then renews on its own. Terraform never re-issues on a plain `apply` — DNS credentials are **write-only** (never stored in state, never diffed). To rotate a token or switch provider, recreate the resource (`terraform apply -replace=...`).

Requires Terraform >= 1.11 / OpenTofu >= 1.9 (write-only arguments).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Certificate display name on the console. Immutable (no rename API) — changing it replaces the certificate.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `active` (Boolean) Whether this certificate is the **active (serving)** console certificate. Defaults to `true` — the resource activates the certificate it installs so the console actually serves it (a freshly issued/uploaded certificate is inactive until activated). Set `false` to install/stage a certificate without serving it.
- `certificate` (String) PEM-encoded certificate (full chain) — required for `source = upload`. Stored and diffed so it chains with an upstream `acme_certificate`/`tls_*` resource: when the PEM changes the certificate is re-uploaded. (The console never returns the PEM, so importing a pre-existing uploaded certificate shows a one-time re-upload diff.)
- `dns_provider` (Attributes, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) DNS provider for automated DNS-01 (`source = letsEncrypt`). The console calls the provider's API itself to place the `_acme-challenge` TXT record. **Write-only**: credentials are consumed at issuance and never stored in state or read back. Use `name = manual` to place the TXT yourself (the device cannot do it for you). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_provider))
- `domain` (String) Fully-qualified domain for the certificate (e.g. `console.example.com`; a wildcard `*.example.com` is allowed). Required for `source = letsEncrypt`. Immutable — changing it replaces the certificate.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) PEM-encoded private key — required for `source = upload`. Write-only: never stored in state.
- `source` (String) How the certificate is obtained: `letsEncrypt` (native ACME via DNS-01; default) or `upload` (bring your own). Immutable — changing it replaces the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `acme_renew_error` (String) Reason the device's last native renewal failed, if any (empty when healthy).
- `cert_version` (Number) Certificate version counter reported by the console (bumps on each native renewal).
- `fingerprint` (String) Certificate fingerprint.
- `id` (String) Console certificate ID. Import key and state `id`.
- `issuer` (String) Issuer common name (CN).
- `serial_number` (String) Certificate serial number.
- `subject_common_name` (String) Subject common name (CN).
- `valid_from` (String) Not-before timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `valid_to` (String) Not-after (expiry) timestamp (RFC 3339). Refreshed on every read; because the device renews natively under the same `id`, expiry drift never produces a plan diff.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_provider"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_provider`

Required:

- `name` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) DNS provider: one of `cloudflare`, `route53`, `godaddy`, `digitalocean`, `porkbun`, `duckdns`, `dynu`, `ovh`, `manual`.

Optional:

- `access_key_id` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Access key ID — `route53`.
- `api_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) API key — `dynu`, `godaddy`, `porkbun`.
- `api_secret` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) API secret — `godaddy`.
- `api_token` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) API token — `cloudflare`, `digitalocean`.
- `application_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Application key — `ovh`.
- `application_secret` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Application secret — `ovh`.
- `consumer_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Consumer key — `ovh`.
- `endpoint` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) API endpoint — `ovh`: one of `ovh-eu`, `ovh-us`, `ovh-ca`, `kimsufi-eu`, `kimsufi-ca`, `soyoustart-eu`, `soyoustart-ca`.
- `region` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Hosted-zone region — `route53`.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Secret access key — `route53`.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Secret key — `porkbun`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Token — `duckdns`.
